aochu,Aochu,青酎,kanto,tokyo,"A rare artisanal sweet potato shochu distilled exclusively on the isolated volcanic island of Aogashima. Crafted by local islanders using indigenous yeast strains and sweet potatoes, it delivers a robust earthy aroma with a complex, velvety finish.",All year,local specialty,Contains none. Vegan-friendly.,2000,5000,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Distilled since the Edo period by island women as a household drink, it evolved into a prized craft spirit shaped by the island's fertile volcanic soil and subtropical climate.",,"Because production is strictly limited to Aogashima's tiny population, it is nationally revered as the phantom shochu.","01 Local Sweet Potatoes

column1: Sun-ripened sweet potatoes harvested from the rich volcanic soil of Aogashima.
Steamed barley inoculated with koji mold to initiate natural starch conversion.
Pure rainfall filtered through porous subterranean layers of volcanic basalt rock.",ah-oh-choo,,"Crystal Clear Spirit
A pristine transparent liquid that presents clean clarity when poured into a glass.
Enclosed in traditional heavy glass bottles featuring distinct island calligraphy seals.
Forms slow-dripping legs along the inner rim of the tasting glass upon swirling.",Link

hingya-no-shio,Hingya no Shio,ひんぎゃの塩,kanto,tokyo,"A mineral-rich gourmet sea salt crystallized using the natural geothermal steam of Aogashima volcano. Deep Kuroshio ocean water is slowly evaporated over gentle volcanic steam vents to yield crunchy, savory salt pyramids.",All year,local specialty,Contains none. Vegan-friendly.,600,1500,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"The name 'Hingya' refers to the volcanic steam vents on the island. This salt-making method harnesses the island's natural geothermal energy, a practice deeply tied to Aogashima's volcanic landscape.",,"It takes weeks of slow evaporation over the volcanic vents to produce this salt, resulting in its signature large, crunchy crystals.","01 Kuroshio Pacific Water

column1: Pure deep ocean water drawn directly from the swift Pacific Kuroshio current.
Naturally occurring calcium and magnesium retained during low-temperature evaporation.",heen-gyah no shee-oh,,"Coarse White Crystals
Fluffy pyramid-shaped white salt crystals showcasing a soft translucent sheen.
Packaged in minimalist brown kraft pouches stamped with official island seals.
Distinctly varied crystal sizes that crumble effortlessly between fingertips.",Link

haijima-highball,Haijima Highball,拝島ハイボール,kanto,tokyo,"A signature local highball crafted in Akishima City using crisp underground spring water. Mixed with quality Japanese whisky and effervescent soda, it offers a clean, ultra-refreshing taste.",All year,local specialty,Contains none. Vegetarian-friendly.,500,900,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Dine-in,Verified vegetarian,Not reviewed,TRUE,"Created to celebrate the local drinking culture around Haijima Station, this highball has become a beloved staple in the area's izakayas.",,Akishima is famous for being the only municipality in Tokyo providing 100% pure underground water for tap supply.,"01 Japanese Blended Whisky

column1: Smooth oak-aged Japanese malt whisky selected for clean aromatic balance.
Highly carbonated sparkling water crafted from pure Akishima deep subterranean wells.
Freshly sliced citrus wedge adding bright acidity and aromatic zest.",hah-ee-jee-mah hye-bohl,,"Effervescent Amber Liquid
Golden amber whisky cocktail brimming with tight carbonation bubbles rising to the top.
Served over crystalline ice blocks in a heavy-bottomed frosted highball glass.
Garnished with a crisp wedge of fresh yellow lemon resting on the ice.",Link

haijima-negi-miso,Haijima Negi Miso,拝島ねぎみそ,kanto,tokyo,A rich savory condiment prepared by sautéing locally grown green onions with aromatic fermented miso paste. It delivers an intense umami punch with sweet caramelized onion notes perfect over warm rice.,All year,local specialty,"Contains Soy, Sesame. Vegan-friendly.",450,850,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Originating as a farmstead preserving method in western Tokyo to extend the shelf life of seasonal scallion harvests.,,This versatile miso paste is commonly spread over rice balls before charcoal grilling to create fragrant yaki-onigiri.,"01 Fresh Haijima Scallions

column1: Locally harvested sweet green onions chopped fine for tender texture.
Aged red and white soy miso paste delivering deep savory depth.
Pure roasted sesame oil added during pan-sautéing for nutty fragrance.",hah-ee-jee-mah neh-gee mee-so,,"Deep Glossy Brown Paste
A thick caramelized dark brown miso paste with visible specks of green scallions.
Sealed inside compact glass jars labeled with traditional Japanese brushed brushwork.
Features tender translucent pieces of diced green onion folded throughout the paste.",Link

akigawa-sweet-corn,Akigawa Sweet Corn,秋川とうもろこし,kanto,tokyo,"Exceptionally sweet and juicy corn cultivated along the fertile riverbanks of the Akigawa Valley in Akiruno City. Plucked early in the morning, these golden kernels are so crisp and sweet they can even be enjoyed raw.",Summer,local specialty,Contains none. Vegan-friendly.,250,500,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,The pure waters of the Akigawa River and the valley's distinct temperature differences create the perfect environment for cultivating this premium corn.,,"During the summer harvest season, you'll find local farmers boiling or grilling these sweet cobs right by the roadside!","01 Fresh Sweet Corn Ears

column1: Morning-harvested sweet corn grown in river mineral soils.
Creamy Hokkaido butter melted over grilled cob ears.
Aged soy sauce brushed over open flame for savory glaze.",ah-kee-gah-wah toh-moh-roh-koh-she,,"Plump Golden Kernels
Tightly packed rows of shiny bright yellow kernels glowing with fresh moisture.
Wrapped in crisp leafy green husks with dark brown corn silk at the tip.
When grilled, features attractive brown char marks coated in glistening melted butter.",Link

norabou-na,Norabou-na,のらぼう菜,kanto,tokyo,"A tender local leafy green with crisp stems and a mild, sweet flavor, traditionally grown in western Tokyo. Norabou-na is valued for its edible stems and leaves and is commonly prepared simply by boiling, blanching, or stir-frying so its fresh green flavor remains clear.",Spring,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",150,400,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Norabou-na is an old Tokyo-area vegetable associated with western suburban farming and has been cultivated in the Akiruno area for generations. Its continued use reflects traditional household vegetable growing and seasonal spring cooking rather than a single inventor.,,"The stalks and leaves can be eaten together, making it less wasteful than greens that require extensive trimming. Harvested stems are especially prized for their tender bite.","01 Norabou-na Leaves

column1: Tender leaves provide a mild green flavor and soft texture.
The thick stems add crispness and remain pleasantly firm after brief cooking.
Soy sauce, sesame, or simple dashi-based seasoning lets the vegetable's sweetness remain noticeable.",noh-rah-boh-nah,,"Long Tender Stems
Sturdy pale-green stems support clusters of soft leaves and are fully edible.
The leaves range from medium to deep green and look succulent rather than fibrous.
A lightly cooked serving keeps the vegetable's natural color and clean, mild appearance.",Link

bunka-fry,Bunka Fry,文化フライ,kanto,tokyo,"A distinctive Adachi street snack made from seasoned wheat dough shaped into a flat, sandal-like form, coated with breadcrumbs, and deep-fried. The finished fritter is lightly sweet, crisp outside, soft inside, and traditionally served hot with a generous amount of special sauce.",All year,local specialty,"Contains wheat, soy",100,300,Published,Quick bite,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,"Bunka Fry was devised by Hasegawa Shoten in Umeda, Adachi Ward, and became a familiar festival-stall snack in the postwar period. It survived mainly through local memory after regular street-stall production declined around 2001.",,"Despite its name, Bunka Fry contains no meat or fish in the basic preparation. It is a flour-based snack whose character comes from the crisp coating, slight sweetness, and savory sauce.","01 Wheat Dough
A simple wheat-flour dough forms the soft, chewy center.
Breadcrumbs create the crisp fried shell and browned exterior.
The signature sauce adds sweetness, saltiness, and concentrated savory flavor.",boon-kah foo-rye,,"Flat Oval Fritter
A thin, elongated fried piece has the characteristic flattened shape.
Fine breadcrumbs form a golden exterior around the soft flour-based center.
A dark, glossy sauce is brushed or poured over the freshly fried snack.",Link

senju-no-suzumeyaki,Senju no Suzumeyaki,千住のすずめ焼き,kanto,tokyo,"A traditional Senju-style small-fish dish in which whole small fish are skewered and grilled with a savory-sweet glaze. The name refers to their small, sparrow-like appearance, while the preparation belongs to the old river-and-market food culture of the Senju area.",All year,local specialty,"Contains fish, soy",500,1200,Published,Dine-in,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,"Suzumeyaki is associated with the historic food culture around Senju, where small freshwater fish were preserved and sold as a practical local food. The surviving style reflects Edo-period riverine cooking rather than a single documented inventor.",,"The name evokes grilled sparrows, but it describes the fish's small appearance, not the bird itself. Eating it with the glaze highlights the contrast between crisp edges and tender fish.","01 Small Freshwater Fish
Small fish such as crucian carp or similar local species form the traditional base.
Soy sauce provides saltiness and umami while developing a dark finish during grilling.
Sugar or mirin balances the glaze and helps it adhere to the fish.",sen-joo no soo-zoo-meh-yah-kee,,"Small Whole Fish
Tiny fish are arranged whole on narrow bamboo skewers.
Repeated brushing gives the grilled fish a deep brown, glossy surface.
The small format makes the dish visually similar to a row of roasted birds.",Link

yarikake-dango,Yarikake Dango,槍かけだんご,kanto,tokyo,"A traditional rice dumpling specialty associated with Senju, formed from chewy rice-flour dumplings on skewers and finished with a sweet or savory topping. The name is linked to a local story about resting a spear, while the dumplings are enjoyed as a simple old-fashioned snack.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",150,500,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Yarikake Dango is tied to the old Senju travel and lodging area and its famous legend about a spear being rested nearby. The dumpling tradition belongs to the historic neighborhood food culture and is preserved through long-running local confectionery shops.,,The name connects the confection to a travel-era story rather than to an ingredient. Freshly made dumplings are at their best while the surface is still soft and the glaze glossy.,"01 Rice Flour Dumplings

column1: Steamed and shaped rice dough provides the soft, chewy body.
Depending on the style, the dumplings may be finished with sweet red bean paste or a savory-sweet glaze.
Sugar balances the toppings and gives the finished skewer its characteristic sweetness.",yah-ree-kah-keh dahn-goh,,"Three-Dumpling Skewer
Round dumplings are lined up closely on a bamboo stick for an immediately recognizable silhouette.
The savory version is coated in a dark, glossy sauce that clings to the rice cakes.
The dumplings retain a smooth, compact surface with a pleasantly chewy bite.",Link

yuyu-toden-wagashi,Yuyu Toden - Wagashi,ゆうゆう都電（和菓子）,kanto,tokyo,"A traditional Japanese confection shaped like the tramcars of the Toden Arakawa Line, created as a playful local souvenir from Arakawa. Sold as a shop-exclusive wagashi in Machiya, it connects a familiar streetcar image with a soft, sweet confectionary format.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, contains wheat",200,600,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Yuyu Toden was developed as a confection associated with the Toden Arakawa Line and is sold exclusively at the Machiya shop of Chikuryuan Okano. Its design turns a well-known Arakawa transport symbol into a local sweet.,,The confection is especially popular with children because the tram shape is easy to recognize. It is also a local souvenir tied directly to the neighborhood where the streetcar runs.,"01 Sweet Bean Filling

column1: Sweet bean paste provides the familiar wagashi center.
A soft Japanese confectionery exterior holds the molded tram shape.
Sugar provides the characteristic sweetness of the finished wagashi.",yoo-yoo toh-den wah-gah-she,,"Tram-Shaped Silhouette
Each confection uses a small streetcar form that is immediately recognizable.
The surface is smooth and carefully molded to hold the vehicle shape.
Individual pieces are sized for easy gifting and casual snacking.",Link

arakawa-monja,Arakawa Monja,あらかわもんじゃ,kanto,tokyo,"A sizzling monjayaki style associated with Arakawa Ward, where a thin dashi-rich batter cooks into a loose, savory mixture on a hot griddle. Cabbage and other ingredients are cooked together, producing the soft texture and concentrated browned edges that define monjayaki.",All year,local specialty,"Contains wheat, soy, various toppings",800,2000,Published,Dine-in,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,"Monjayaki became deeply established in Tokyo's working-class neighborhoods, and Arakawa developed its own local eating culture around the dish. The ward's style reflects the broader shitamachi tradition rather than a single inventor.",,"A tiny metal spatula is used both to cook and eat monjayaki. The most prized bites are often the small, crisp pieces that form against the griddle.","01 Dashi-Flavored Batter
A thin mixture of flour and dashi creates the characteristic loose texture.
Finely chopped cabbage adds sweetness, moisture, and texture.
Seafood, meat, vegetables, cheese, or other additions create the chosen flavor profile.",ah-rah-kah-wah mon-jah,,"Hot Iron Griddle
The dish is cooked directly on a tabletop griddle and served bubbling hot.
A thin batter surrounds finely cut cabbage and other chosen fillings.
Small browned patches form where the mixture contacts the hot plate.",Link

okara-soy-milk-karinto,Okara & Soy Milk Karinto,おからと豆乳のかりんとう,kanto,tokyo,"A crunchy karinto made with okara and soy milk, turning familiar soybean by-products into a sweet, crisp snack. The version produced by Nakano Confectionery in Itabashi is recognized locally for its practical use of soy ingredients and its light, pleasantly crumbly bite.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, contains soy, wheat",300,700,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"The product is made by Nakano Confectionery and is listed among Itabashi's recognized local specialty foods. Its concept combines traditional karinto-making with okara and soy milk, reflecting an effort to use more of the soybean after tofu production.",,Okara is the soybean pulp left after making soy milk or tofu. Using it in confectionery gives the snack a distinctive crumb and turns a tofu-making by-product into part of the finished food.,"01 Okara

column1: Soybean pulp adds body and a slightly nutty, crumbly character.
Soy milk enriches the dough and reinforces the soybean flavor.
Flour provides structure while sugar supplies the characteristic sweetness of karinto.",oh-kah-rah to toh-nyoo no kah-reen-toh,,"Slim Fried Sticks
Short, narrow pieces show the irregular handmade character of the snack.
The fried surface develops a warm golden color without a heavy coating.
The pieces have a firm exterior that breaks cleanly when bitten.",Link

niku-no-marusan-homemade-ham-cutlet,Niku no Marusan Homemade Ham Cutlet,肉のマルサン 自家製ハムカツ,kanto,tokyo,"A thick, butcher-shop-style ham cutlet made from a substantial slice of ham, coated and fried until the outside is crisp and golden. Niku no Marusan in Kamitabashi sells this house-made version as one of the products recognized by the Itabashi local specialty program.",All year,local specialty,"Contains meat, wheat, egg",150,400,Published,Quick bite,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,"Ham cutlets became a familiar Japanese butcher-shop food during the twentieth century, and Niku no Marusan developed its own house-made version for its Kamitabashi customers. The shop's cutlet was later selected for Itabashi's local specialty program.",,"Niku no Marusan is a neighborhood butcher that also prepares cooked foods in-house. The ham cutlet is designed as an everyday, ready-to-eat side rather than a formal restaurant dish.","01 Ham
A thick slice of cured ham supplies the savory center.
The standard cutlet coating uses flour and egg to help the crumbs adhere.
Japanese breadcrumbs create the crisp, light-textured crust after frying.",nee-koo no mah-roo-sahn hah-moo-kah-tsoo,,"Thick Ham Center
The cutlet shows a noticeably generous interior of sliced ham rather than a paper-thin filling.
A crisp breadcrumb coating forms an even fried shell around the ham.
The cutlet is best shown hot and freshly fried, when the crust is most delicate.",Link

inagi-pears,Inagi Pears,稲城の梨,kanto,tokyo,"Large, juicy Japanese pears grown in Inagi, a long-established pear-growing area in Tokyo. Local fruit is prized for abundant juice, pronounced sweetness, and a crisp texture, with farm stands becoming especially busy during the harvest period from late summer into autumn.",Fall,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",500,3000,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Pear cultivation in Inagi is traced by the city to the Genroku era, when two local men are said to have brought back a pear cultivar from the Kyoto region. Commercial production became established later in the nineteenth century, leading to today's regional brand.",,The city says local pear stalls begin appearing prominently around mid-August. Inagi pears are also widely purchased as gifts and shipped outside Tokyo during the harvest season.,"01 Japanese Pears

column1: Crisp Japanese pears provide the signature juicy sweetness and clean aroma.
Fruit is harvested at orchard ripeness for direct sale and local distribution.
The pear's high natural juice content creates the refreshing texture associated with the Inagi brand.",ee-nah-gee no nah-she,,"Large Round Fruit
Inagi pears are often notably large and round compared with many supermarket pears.
The cut surface is pale, firm, and visibly juicy.
Smooth skin and a clean stem end emphasize the freshness expected from direct farm sales.",Link

inagi-mukashibanashi-manju,Inagi Mukashibanashi Manju,稲城の昔ばなしまんじゅう,kanto,tokyo,"A soft Japanese steamed bun created as an Inagi souvenir around local folktales and storytelling. The confection pairs a tender outer cake with a sweet filling, turning the city's traditional narratives into a compact gift suitable for visitors and everyday tea service.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, contains wheat",150,500,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"The confection was developed as a local Inagi souvenir inspired by the city's traditional folktales. Its purpose is cultural as well as culinary, using wagashi to give local stories a portable form.",,The phrase old folktales refers to traditional local stories passed between generations. The manju turns that cultural theme into a food souvenir rather than representing a single historic recipe.,"01 Wheat Flour

column1: Flour forms the soft steamed outer cake.
Sweet bean paste supplies the traditional wagashi-style filling.
Sugar balances the filling and dough and gives the manju its gentle sweetness.",ee-nah-gee moo-kah-she-bah-nah-she mahn-joo,,"Round Steamed Bun
The small, rounded form gives the confection the familiar silhouette of a manju.
A decorative mark or printed design connects the sweet with Inagi's folktale theme.
The cut surface reveals a smooth sweet filling inside the tender cake.",Link

komatsuna,Komatsuna,小松菜,kanto,tokyo,"A dark green leafy vegetable strongly associated with Edogawa, where the Komatsugawa area gave the crop its name. Komatsuna has crisp stems and a mild sweetness, and today it is grown year-round, although its original peak season is winter when cool weather intensifies its flavor.",Winter,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",100,300,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Komatsuna's name is traditionally linked to the eighth shogun Tokugawa Yoshimune, who is said to have eaten local winter greens during a hawking visit and named them after Komatsugawa. Historical texts later confirm the reputation of the vegetable in the area.",,"Komatsuna can be harvested several times a year in modern cultivation, but winter remains its traditional season. Frost is said to make the leaves sweeter and more flavorful.","01 Komatsuna Leaves

column1: The dark leaves provide a mild mustardy note and high vegetable freshness.
Crisp stems give the vegetable its characteristic crunch.
Cool-season growth concentrates sweetness, especially in traditional winter crops.",koh-mah-tsoo-nah,,"Deep Green Leaves
Broad, dark leaves create a fresh, substantial appearance.
The thick stems remain crunchy and add contrast to the softer leaves.
Whole plants are commonly sold with stems intact to preserve freshness.",Link

salad-komatsuna,Salad Komatsuna,サラダ小松菜,kanto,tokyo,"A tender, mild form of komatsuna developed specifically for comfortable raw eating, with less bitterness and more perceived sweetness than traditional mature greens. The product was developed through an Edogawa agricultural-academic-public partnership and is marketed for salads, juices, and other uncooked uses.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",150,400,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Salad Komatsuna was developed through a joint Edogawa agricultural, academic, and public-sector project studying the safety and nutritional value of eating komatsuna raw. After two years of research, the product was commercialized as a milder salad-oriented form.",,"The project specifically tested raw-eating suitability, which is why this version is much less assertive in taste than mature cooking greens. It can also be blended directly into juice.","01 Salad Komatsuna

column1: Tender leaves provide a mild flavor designed for raw eating.
The young stems add fresh crunch without requiring boiling.
A sweeter taste helps the greens work in salads and fresh juices.",sah-rah-dah koh-mah-tsoo-nah,,"Tender Bright Leaves
Leaves appear softer and more delicate than mature cooking komatsuna.
The stems remain crisp but are fine enough to eat raw.
Whole leaves are easy to arrange in salads without lengthy trimming or cooking.",Link

ome-senbei,Ome Senbei,青梅せんべい,kanto,tokyo,"A traditional rice-cracker-style confection associated with Ome, known for its light sweetness and crisp, delicate bite. The local souvenir is shaped and baked into thin pieces that travel well, making it a familiar tea-time gift from western Tokyo.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, contains wheat",300,1000,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Ome Senbei is a long-standing local confection associated with the city's souvenir culture rather than a single documented inventor. Its style reflects the broader Japanese tradition of crisp baked sweets made for tea and gifting.,,The crackers are particularly suited to tea because their modest sweetness lets the roasted grain aroma remain noticeable. Their dry texture also makes them easy to carry as a travel souvenir.,"01 Rice Flour

column1: Rice provides the crisp, light structure associated with senbei.
A small amount of wheat-based flour contributes structure in the local recipe.
Sugar gives the cracker its gently sweet finish.",oh-meh sen-bay,,"Thin Pale Cracker
The finished senbei is thin, light, and lightly browned.
Many pieces have a gentle curve that makes them visually distinctive.
The crackers are commonly presented as stackable souvenir pieces for tea service.",Link

noshikon,Noshikon,のしこん,kanto,tokyo,"A locally made konnyaku specialty associated with Ome, produced in thin rolled sheets rather than the standard rectangular blocks. The translucent pieces have a springy, pleasantly firm texture and are typically served chilled with a savory sauce or alongside other simple Japanese foods.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",200,500,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Noshikon is a specialized local konnyaku product whose name comes from its rolled form. It belongs to Ome's regional food tradition of working with konnyaku as a practical, low-cost staple ingredient.",,"Konnyaku has almost no inherent flavor, so texture is the main attraction. Chilling the slices and adding a concentrated dipping sauce makes the springy bite more pronounced.","01 Konnyaku Flour

column1: Konnyaku powder provides the gelatinous, elastic base.
Water hydrates the konnyaku flour and creates the final firm gel texture.
A traditional alkaline ingredient helps the konnyaku mixture set into a stable gel.",noh-she-kon,,"Translucent Rolled Sheets
Thin sheets of konnyaku show a clear, slightly gray appearance.
The pieces hold their shape while revealing the characteristic elastic bite of konnyaku.
Sliced portions are easy to serve with dipping sauce or as a light side dish.",Link

bekko-sushi,Bekko Sushi,べっこう寿司,kanto,tokyo,"A distinctive island sushi from Izu Oshima made by marinating slices of local fish in a sweet-savory soy sauce before placing them over vinegared rice. The marinade gives the fish a glossy amber-brown appearance, which explains the name referring to tortoiseshell.",All year,local specialty,"Contains fish, soy",1000,2000,Published,Dine-in,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,Bekko sushi developed as a practical island preparation for seasoning fish with soy sauce and keeping its flavor appealing. The style became characteristic of Oshima's food culture and is now treated as one of the island's representative dishes.,,"The name bekko refers to tortoiseshell, a reference to the amber-brown shine created by the soy marinade. In Oshima, mustard is traditionally preferred with the sushi instead of wasabi.","01 Local White Fish
Fish such as sawara is sliced thinly for marinating.
Soy sauce provides saltiness, umami, and the characteristic amber color.
Lightly sweetened vinegared rice balances the savory fish and marinade.",bek-koh zoo-she,,"Amber-Marinated Fish
Thin fish slices develop a deep, translucent brown sheen from the marinade.
Each slice sits neatly over a small mound of seasoned rice.
The restrained arrangement highlights the fish's color and glossy surface.",Link

zako-teishoku,Zako Teishoku,ざこ定食,kanto,tokyo,"A casual island set meal built around small local fish, often served grilled, fried, or simmered with rice and everyday side dishes. The concept reflects Oshima's practical seafood cooking, where modest catches are turned into a satisfying complete meal rather than treated as luxury ingredients.",All year,local specialty,"Contains fish, soy",800,1500,Published,Dine-in,Not reviewed,Not reviewed,FALSE,Zako teishoku is best understood as a local set-meal style using small fish rather than as one fixed historical recipe. Its roots lie in Oshima's fishing households and the practical use of readily available catches.,,"The word zako refers broadly to small fish rather than one exact species. Because the term is flexible, the fish and preparation can vary with the day's catch and the restaurant.","01 Small Local Fish
The day's small catch provides the central protein and can be grilled, fried, or simmered.
Plain rice provides a neutral base for the strongly flavored fish.
Soup and small vegetable dishes complete the balanced set-meal format.",zah-koh tay-shoh-koo,,"Local Fish Main
A plate of simply prepared small fish anchors the meal.
Steamed rice, soup, and small seasonal sides create the visual structure of a Japanese set meal.
Simple ceramics and separated portions emphasize the everyday island character.",Link

gyunu-senbei,Gyunu Senbei,牛乳せんべい,kanto,tokyo,"A crisp, lightly sweet milk biscuit from Izu Oshima, made into thin baked pieces that pair naturally with tea or coffee. The simple recipe reflects the island's dairy connection and produces a dry, fragrant snack with a delicate snap.",All year,local specialty,"Contains dairy, wheat, egg",400,1000,Published,Vegetarian
column3: Quick bite,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,Milk Senbei became established as an Oshima souvenir using the island's dairy connection and the Japanese tradition of producing crisp baked gift sweets. The exact commercial origin is associated with local confectionery makers rather than a single national inventor.,,"Despite its name, milk senbei is closer to a thin sweet biscuit than a savory rice cracker. The milky aroma becomes more noticeable when the biscuit is eaten with a warm drink.","01 Wheat Flour

column1: Wheat flour provides the biscuit's structure.
Milk gives the cracker its gentle dairy aroma and pale finish.
Sugar adds the restrained sweetness typical of the confection.",gyoo-nyoo sen-bay,,"Thin Baked Discs
Light-colored biscuits are baked into flat, crisp pieces.
The interior has a delicate, dry structure rather than a dense cookie crumb.
The biscuits are easy to stack and pack, making them a classic island souvenir.",Link

omori-nori,Omori Nori,大森の海苔,kanto,tokyo,"A historic nori-producing tradition from Omori, where calm, nutrient-rich Tokyo Bay waters once supported one of Japan's major seaweed-growing areas. Although cultivation ended in the 1960s, Omori remains a major center for nori wholesalers, grading, processing, and distribution.",All year,local specialty,"Vegan, Gluten-free",500,3000,Published,Vegetarian
column2: Halal,Verified vegetarian,Verified halal,TRUE,"Nori cultivation began along the Omori-to-Shinagawa coast about three centuries ago, and Omori became a leading production area from the Meiji era through the early Showa period. Cultivation ended in 1963 after fishing rights were relinquished amid coastal development, but the local trade continued.",,Omori was once important enough to spread nori cultivation and processing techniques to other parts of Japan. Today the area's nori wholesalers still judge and process seaweed from production regions around the country.,"01 Edible Seaweed

column1: Porphyra-type seaweed forms the raw material for dried nori sheets.
The sea environment influences the mineral content and flavor of the growing seaweed.
Gentle roasting develops the characteristic crisp texture and nutty aroma.",oh-moh-ree no-ree,,"Deep Green Sheets
Quality nori shows a dark green to nearly black surface with fine, even texture.
